The Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde’s Allied Peoples Movement Presidential Campaign Organisation has criticised President Bola Tinubu over the federal government’s embargo on recruitment, describing the decision as insensitive to the plight of Nigerians, particularly youths seeking employment opportunities. The organisation, in a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, on Tuesday, said the recruitment freeze contradicted the All Progressives Congress-led Federal Government’s promises on job creation, arguing that the policy widened the gap between its public commitments and actions. The Federal Government instructed Ministries, Departments and Agencies to retain their current workforce levels in 2027, warning that those that fail to provide staff records and justify their personnel budget requests risk losing approval for their staff strength and budgetary allocations. It also barred federal institutions from recruiting additional workers or expanding their structures without clearance from the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation. The directives were contained in a November 9, 2026, circular titled ‘2027 Workforce Budget Call Circular’, signed by the Permanent Secretary, Service Policies and Strategies Office, Ishiyaku Musa Mohammed. It stated, “The employment embargo comes as a damning indictment of President Tinubu’s economic policies and a glaring contradiction of the All Progressives Congress (APC)’s much-publicised promises on job creation, thus showing a wide gap between policy rhetoric and the real intentions of the government. “This ill-conceived recruitment freeze clearly offers a glimpse into the inner workings of the Tinubu administration’s faltering economic policies, with the more alarming prospect being a likely precursor to possible mass retrenchment in the public service under the guise of fiscal discipline, should President Tinubu secure re-election in 2027. “The gravity of this situation becomes significant when considered against the country’s labour market realities. The World Bank estimates that approximately 3.5 million Nigerians enter the labour market annually. “It is unpardonable that while leaders in other climes are growing their economies by transparently and effectively harnessing their natural and human capital resources and creating employment opportunities for their citizens, President Tinubu is abandoning millions of Nigeria’s hardworking youths in the labour market because of his manifest lack of ideas and capacity to lead.” The campaign organisation also faulted the Federal Government’s justification for imposing a recruitment embargo, describing as outrageous its claim that the move would consolidate public service reforms and help determine personnel needs for the 2027 budget. It added, “If indeed President Tinubu knows his onions as a leader, he would have used his position to create a governance system that would have effectively harnessed our vast national and human resources, maximised our productive capacity, expanded the economy and created millions of new jobs instead of placing an embargo on employment. “It is obvious that this administration has no intention of making life better for Nigerians, hence the declaration by the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul-Aziz Yari, that Nigerians complaining of hunger and hardship are lazy. “We caution Nigerians that an administration which came to power promising economic renewal and job creation but now responds to the country’s unemployment crisis by further restricting recruitment opportunities has driven itself into an economic cul-de-sac and must be helped out of office before it completely ruins the future of the nation. “Instead of denying Nigerians opportunities and the right to federal government employment, President Tinubu should take a cue from the Oyo State success story under the leadership of the Presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement, Engr. Seyi Makinde, whose policies and programmes resulted in unprecedented wealth creation, economic revolution and mass employment in various sectors of the state’s economy.” Abdulrahman Zakariyau Abdulrahman is a journalist at Punch Newspapers with nearly a decade of professional experience covering political parties, elections, religion, civil society organizations, and the Nigeria Governors Forum.
